subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin-facing pre-apply veto for persisted config writes, and what ordering, metadata, and failure semantics should that public API expose?
rationale: This would define a public plugin API around security-sensitive persisted config writes, so automation cannot safely choose fail-open/fail-closed behavior, SecretRef ordering, recursion rules, metadata contract, timeout behavior, or SDK boundary.

options.title: Design the API first
options.body: Keep this issue open, settle hook ordering and metadata in maintainer design, then implement the agreed SDK contract with regression tests proving rejection leaves disk and active runtime config unchanged.

options.title: Rely on built-in validation
options.body: Decline a plugin veto API and rescope safety work to schema validation, SecretRef preflight, semantic model/provider validation, baseHash guards, destructive-array checks, and agent-tool allowlists.

options.title: Limit interception to agent writes
options.body: Add a narrower guard around model-initiated gateway config writes while accepting that CLI, setup, Control UI, and shared helper writes remain outside the plugin veto path.

recommendation.title: Design the API first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, settle hook ordering and metadata in maintainer design, then implement the agreed SDK contract with regression tests proving rejection leaves disk and active runtime config unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: They already provided the clearest product-routing review on this issue and are the strongest current discussion owner for the API/security boundary.
